# zeroword_domain (Resource)

A custom Hosted Login domain of an Environment. Publish the TXT record `verification_record_name` = `verification_record_value` (for example with a DNS provider resource); Zeroword activates the domain after it sees the record.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "zeroword_domain" "login" {
  environment_id = zeroword_environment.staging.id
  hostname       = "login.example.com"
}

# Publish the ownership TXT record, e.g. with Cloudflare.
resource "cloudflare_dns_record" "zeroword_login" {
  zone_id = var.cloudflare_zone_id
  name    = zeroword_domain.login.verification_record_name
  type    = "TXT"
  content = zeroword_domain.login.verification_record_value
  ttl     = 300
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID (`env_...`).
- `hostname` (String) Custom hostname, e.g. `login.example.com`.

### Optional

- `rp_enabled` (Boolean) Also serve this host as the WebAuthn RP ID. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Domain ID.
- `ownership_verified` (Boolean) Whether the TXT record was found.
- `status` (String) Provisioning status.
- `verification_record_name` (String) TXT record name to publish.
- `verification_record_value` (String) TXT record value to publish.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import zeroword_domain.login dom_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```
